Team —

Triage notes:
- Root cause appears to be a misconfigured project -> tier alias added during last weeks onboarding. The alias (medsync-mobile-prd) was accidentally mapped to the org-default tier for a sandbox cluster instead of the enterprise tier.
- The policy engine applies org->project tiering at request-routing time; that mapping error means their effective per-project quota dropped by ~80%.
- We see a retry storm from the MedSync SDK (exponential backoff misconfigured to aggressive immediate retries). Combined with the quota hit that produced a positive feedback loop.

Action taken: increased their effective quota for medsync-mobile-prd, added temporary burst tokens, and enabled prefix caching for recurring requests. Coordinating a controlled rollback of the alias mapping now.

Monica
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Markus / team —

Investigated: the alias medsync-mobile-prd was introduced by an onboarding script during a customer automation run (deploy id deploy-20260818-47). The mapping accidentally referenced the sandbox-tier id (tier-sbx-7) instead of enterprise-tier-id (tier-ent-2) due to a variable interpolation bug. The change propagated at 07:24 PDT and the routing decision started applying at 07:25.

Mitigations performed:
- Re-mapped medsync-mobile-prd to tier-ent-2 (effective 07:40 PDT).
- Issued temporary quota uplift and burst tokens to absorb the retry wave.
- Added a throttle smoothing rule to reduce instant failures and give clients room for backoff.

Next steps: hotfix onboarding script to validate tier ids (patch ready), add a preflight that simulates traffic tier assignment, and add telemetry alerts to detect large drop-offs in effective per-project quotas. I can push the onboarding patch in 2 hours.

-Rishi
SRE, Inference Routing
